mainTopic: Where does the תורה teach שליחות for תרומה, גירושין and קדשים, and what do the words 'גם אתם' teach?
overview: The גמרא finishes a משנה showing that a שליח can separate תרומה, and asks for the source. Learning it from גירושין fails, because גירושין is חול, so the פסוק 'גם אתם' is brought to include a שליח. Next comes a משנה showing that a שליח can slaughter a קרבן פסח for a group. The source for that is רבי יהושע בן קרחה's famous rule, שלוחו של אדם כמותו. No single case can teach another, because each has its own special feature. When the גמרא tries learning one case from the other two, קדשים and גירושין fail, but תרומה can be learned from them. That frees 'גם אתם' to teach רבי ינאי's rule that a שליח must be one of the בני ברית. The גמרא defends that need against רבי יוחנן's principle and against the view of רבי שמעון. Finally it asks how רבי יונתן, who reads the פסח פסוק differently, learns שליחות for קדשים, and his ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A messenger's slightly-off amount still counts as תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה: if the שליח took ten less or ten more than the average measure, his תרומה is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the messenger went down by ten or up by ten, his תרומה is still תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a משנה about a שליח who separates תרומה. This משנה is the evidence that a שליח can separate תרומה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual average is one out of fifty. If the שליח took one out of forty or one out of sixty, his separation still works. This shows that שליחות works for תרומה, and it sets up the question of where that rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: If he subtracted ten or added ten,
phrases.notes: The usual amount is one out of fifty. Going down ten means one out of forty, and going up ten means one out of sixty.

phrases.english: his teruma is teruma.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח's separation of תרומה is valid even if he takes a little more or less than the average amount.

steps.title: What is the source for a messenger separating תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source and suggests it might be learned from גירושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? And if you would say we learn it from divorce...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that a שליח can separate תרומה. It proposes learning it from גירושין, where we already know שליחות works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes that שליחות works for תרומה, so the גמרא wants a source. The first idea is a comparison to גירושין. The very next line will reject that idea.

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?
And if you would say that it is learned from divorce,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that שליחות works for separating תרומה.

steps.title: Divorce is a non-sacred matter, so it cannot teach about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Learning from גירושין fails, because גירושין is חול, while תרומה is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about divorce is that it is a non-sacred matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning from גירושין. Divorce is an ordinary, non-holy matter, and holy matters might have stricter rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agency may be allowed for חול matters like גירושין. That does not prove it is allowed for something holy like תרומה, so the comparison breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: what about... (opening a reason why two cases are different)

phrases.english: What about divorce?
It is a non-sacred matter!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed comparison of תרומה to גירושין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: גירושין is חול, so it cannot teach a rule for a holy matter like תרומה.

steps.title: The extra word 'also' includes a messenger
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'אתם' and then 'גם אתם'. The extra word teaches that a שליח can separate תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'you', and also 'you also', to include the messenger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a direct source in the פסוק about תרומה. The extra word 'גם' adds a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source does not come from a comparison. It comes straight from the words of the פסוק about תרומה, so the difference between חול and holy matters no longer matters.
steps.whatToRemember: שליחות for תרומה comes from 'גם אתם', not from גירושין.

phrases.english: The verse says: "you,"
"you also":
this includes the messenger.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'גם' in 'גם אתם' includes a שליח for separating תרומה.

steps.title: Why not write it only by תרומה and learn the rest from there?
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה teaches שליחות by תרומה, why not learn גירושין and קידושין from תרומה, instead of writing a separate source for each?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Merciful One write it only regarding תרומה, and let these other cases come and learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges why the תורה needs separate sources for שליחות. One source by תרומה could teach all the other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something holy like תרומה should be the stricter case. If שליחות works there, it should surely work for חול matters like גירושין and קידושין, so the other sources look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: let the Merciful One (the תורה) write
and let them learn from it

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write it regarding teruma,
and let these others come and learn from it!
phrases.notes: "These others" are divorce and betrothal, which the גמרא discussed just before this.

steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate sources for שליחות in גירושין and קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source by תרומה should be enough to teach the other cases.

steps.title: תרומה is special because it works with thought alone
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn from תרומה, because תרומה can take effect with מחשבה alone. So it is more lenient in a way the other cases are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one can refute it: תרומה can take effect through thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other cases cannot be learned from תרומה. תרומה has a unique leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since תרומה works with just a decision in the mind, maybe its flexibility with a שליח is also unique to it. That is why גירושין and קידושין need their own sources.
steps.confusionAlert: Here תרומה is called the more lenient case, even though it is holy. Each comparison looks at a different feature.

phrases.english: Because it can be refuted:
for it can take effect through thought.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה could serve as the single source for all שליחות.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה works with מחשבה, so the other cases cannot be learned from it.

steps.title: A messenger slaughters the lost קרבן פסח for the group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a group sent one member to find and slaughter their lost פסח. If his animal was slaughtered first, they all eat from his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding what we learned: a group lost its פסח and told one person to go search and slaughter for them. He found it and slaughtered it, and they also took another animal and slaughtered it. If his was slaughtered first, he eats from his, and they eat and drink with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case where שליחות works, the קרבן פסח. This sets up the next question about its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The member's slaughter counts for the whole group because he acted as their שליח. So שליחות works even for קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: and that which we learned in a משנה
a group registered for one קרבן פסח

phrases.english: And that which we learned:
A group whose Paschal offering was lost,
and they said to one person:
"Go and search, and slaughter it on our behalf,"
and he went, found it, and slaughtered it,
and they took another and slaughtered it,
if his was slaughtered first,
he eats from his,
and they eat and drink with him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח can slaughter the קרבן פסח for a group, and his slaughter counts for them.

steps.title: What is the source for a messenger with קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of שליחות in the קרבן פסח and suggests learning it from the earlier cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? And if you would say it is learned from these...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that a שליח can slaughter a קרבן. It suggests learning it from גירושין and תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal is to learn קדשים from the cases already discussed. The next line will show why that comparison fails.

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?
And if you would say it is learned from these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the earlier cases of שליחות, like divorce and תרומה.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that שליחות works for slaughtering קדשים.

steps.title: The earlier cases are non-sacred compared to offerings
steps.stepSummary: Learning from גירושין and תרומה fails, because they are חול compared to קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about these is that they are non-sacred compared to offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning קדשים from the earlier cases. Even תרומה counts as חול next to קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים are on a higher level of holiness and may have stricter rules. So שליחות in lower cases does not prove it works for קרבנות. The next step gives קדשים its own source.
steps.whatToRemember: Holiness comes in levels. תרומה is holy compared to גירושין, but חול compared to קדשים, so each needs its own source for שליחות.

phrases.english: What about these?
They are non-sacred compared to offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ, שֶׁכֵּן יֶשְׁנָן חוֹל אֵצֶל קָדָשִׁים
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning שליחות for קדשים from גירושין and תרומה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those cases are חול compared to קדשים, so they cannot teach a rule for offerings.

steps.title: The source for agency in the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: שליחות in קדשים is learned from רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reading of the פסוק about slaughtering the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who said: How do we know a person's agent is like himself? The פסוק says, "The whole assembly of Israel shall slaughter it in the afternoon." Does the whole assembly really slaughter? Only one person slaughters! So we learn from here that a person's agent is like himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8: the source for שליחות in the קרבן פסח is a פסוק that speaks of everyone slaughtering, even though only one person does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says all of Israel slaughters, but in real life one person slaughters for the group. The only way that makes sense is that the one who slaughters acts as everyone's agent, so his act counts as theirs. That gives קדשים its own source for שליחות.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's agent is like himself
The assembly of the congregation of Israel

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the general rule שלוחו של אדם כמותו, which is quoted throughout ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה,
phrases.english: He derives it from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
From where do we know that a person's agent is like himself?
As it says: "And they shall slaughter it,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל קְהַל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel, in the afternoon."
Does the whole assembly, all of them, slaughter?
But only one person slaughters!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִכָּאן שֶׁשְּׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: Rather, from here we learn that a person's agent is like himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 rejected learning קדשים from חול cases, this gives קדשים its own פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does שליחות in קדשים come from?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the פסוק 'ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל', since only one person actually slaughters for everyone.

steps.title: Why not write agency only for offerings?
steps.stepSummary: If קדשים has a source, let the תורה write שליחות only there and learn the other cases from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Merciful One write it only by קדשים, and let these other cases come and learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: why does the תורה need several sources? One source in קדשים should be enough for everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is to save extra פסוקים. If שליחות works in קדשים, it should also work for גירושין, קידושין, and תרומה, so the extra sources look unnecessary.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write it by offerings,
and let these come and learn from it!
phrases.notes: "These" means the other cases of agency: גירושין, קידושין and תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּקָדָשִׁים, וְנֵיתֵי הָנָךְ וְנִיגְמְרוּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source just given for קדשים to question the need for the other sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate sources for שליחות in each area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source in קדשים could teach all the other cases, so the extra sources seem unnecessary.

steps.title: Offerings are mostly done through agents
steps.stepSummary: קדשים cannot teach the other cases, because most of their service is done by an agent anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one can push back: What about קדשים? Most of their actions are done through an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that קדשים is a special case, so the other areas cannot be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים, agency is the normal way things are done: the כהנים do the service for the owner. A system built on agents might accept שליחות more easily, so that does not prove שליחות works for divorce or marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: One can refute (push back on the comparison)
What about X, that it has (a special feature)

phrases.english: Because one can refute:
What about offerings?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן רוֹב מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ.
phrases.english: Most of their actions are done through an agent.
phrases.notes: Think of the כהנים, who do most of the work of a קרבן on behalf of the owner.

steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא: pointing out a special feature of the source case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One source in קדשים could teach all the cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים is unusual because agency is its normal way of working, so it cannot teach the others.

steps.title: Learn one case from the other two
steps.stepSummary: No single case can teach another, but maybe two cases together can teach the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: One cannot be learned from one. But let one be learned from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that no single case teaches another, then tries a new approach: combine two cases to teach the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each single comparison failed because of a special feature. When two different cases both allow שליחות, the special feature of one is not found in the other, so together they might show that שליחות works everywhere. That would make one source unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: One cannot be learned from one
Let one be learned from two

phrases.english: One cannot be learned from one,
so let one be learned from two?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the single-case rejections (steps 6, 9, 12) and proposes combining two sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for three separate sources
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources together can cancel out each one's special feature, so the third source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Which case would be learned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the three cases would be the one learned from the other two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one would be learned?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move: the גמרא will test each option one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To check the two-case idea, the גמרא has to try each case as the one being learned. If every option fails, all the sources are needed.

phrases.english: Which one would be learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining the proposal of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case would be learned from the other two?

steps.title: Offerings cannot be learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: קדשים cannot be learned from גירושין and תרומה, because both of those are חול compared to קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Merciful One not write it by קדשים, and learn it from these? What about these: they are חול compared to קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, learning קדשים from the other two, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even תרומה is not holy compared to קרבנות, so both teaching cases share a feature קדשים lacks. Since both share the same weakness, combining them does not help, and קדשים might have stricter rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Not holy, compared to holy offerings

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it by offerings
and let it be learned from these?
What about these?
They are non-sacred compared to offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּקָדָשִׁים וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first option raised by step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning קדשים from גירושין and תרומה together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both teaching cases are חול relative to קדשים, a weakness they share, so combining them does not help.

steps.title: Divorce cannot be learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: גירושין cannot be learned from תרומה and קדשים, because both of those can take effect through thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Merciful One not write it by גירושין, and learn it from these? What about these: they can take effect through thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, learning גירושין from the other two, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תרומה and קדשים can be set aside just by thinking, which makes them easier to bring into effect. גירושין needs a real act, so a rule that works in those cases may not carry over to divorce.
steps.whatToRemember: These first two options fail because the two teaching cases share a feature the third lacks: קדשים is holier than the other two, and גירושין needs an action while the other two can work through thought. The third option, תרומה, is tested next.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it by divorce
and let it be learned from these?
What about these?
They can take effect through thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּגֵירוּשִׁין וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the next option after step 15 failed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning גירושין from תרומה and קדשים together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both teaching cases can take effect through thought, a leniency גירושין does not have.

steps.title: Maybe תרומה is the case learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting קדשים and גירושין as the learned case, the גמרא proposes the third option: the תורה need not write שליחות for תרומה, since it could be learned from קדשים and גירושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let the תורה not write the rule of agency for תרומה, and let us learn it from these two (קדשים and גירושין)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last remaining option. Maybe תרומה is the case that can be learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15 and 16 showed that קדשים and גירושין cannot be learned from the other two. The objections that sank those options do not work against תרומה. גירושין is even more חול than תרומה, and קדשים is holier than תרומה yet still allows a שליח. Also, קדשים, like תרומה, can take effect through thought. So the תורה's פסוק about תרומה seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
and let it be learned from these
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rather, let the Merciful One not write it about תרומה,
phrases.notes: "It" means the rule that you can use an agent.

phrases.english: and let it be learned from these!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּתְרוּמָה, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the third and last option after steps 15 and 16 ruled out the first two.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the תורה's פסוק about שליחות in תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If תרומה can be learned from קדשים and גירושין together, the verse about תרומה seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Yes, תרומה is indeed learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: the rule of agency for תרומה really can be learned from קדשים and גירושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, that is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the suggestion: yes, תרומה is learned from the other two. This answer sets up the next question, because now the verse about תרומה seems to have nothing left to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a concession, not a defense. The derivation for תרומה now comes from the two other cases. But the words "אתם גם אתם" were used earlier to include a שליח for תרומה. Those words now seem unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is so (agreeing with the point)

phrases.english: Indeed, that is so.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the גמרא accepts the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed a separate verse to teach שליחות for תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שליחות for תרומה is learned from קדשים and גירושין together.

steps.title: Then why do we need the words "גם אתם"?
steps.stepSummary: If תרומה is learned from the other cases, the extra word "גם" that seemed to include an agent for תרומה is now unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need "you" and "you also"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the result it just accepted. If תרומה's agency comes from the other two cases, what is the extra word "גם" in the פסוק teaching us?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, "גם אתם" was read as adding an agent for תרומה. Step 18 made that reading unnecessary. The תורה does not waste words, so "גם" must teach something else.

phrases.english: But then why do I need "you" and "you also"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:28. Earlier, the extra word "גם" was used to include an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from accepting step 18: the verse now seems extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The purpose of the extra words "גם אתם".
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If agency for תרומה is already learned from other cases, the extra word in the פסוק teaches nothing.

steps.title: "גם אתם" teaches that an agent must be a Jew
steps.stepSummary: The words are needed for רבי ינאי's rule. Just as the senders are בני ברית, their agents must also be בני ברית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רבי ינאי's teaching. For רבי ינאי said: "You also" means that just as you are members of the covenant, your agents must also be members of the covenant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the extra words a new job. They teach who is allowed to be an agent for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse no longer teaches that agency works. It teaches the requirements for a valid agent. The agent must be like the sender, a member of the covenant. So a נכרי cannot separate תרומה on behalf of a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of the covenant, meaning Jews
It is needed for (a different teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of agency for תרומה comes from קדשים and גירושין together. "גם אתם" teaches that the agent must be a Jew.

phrases.english: It is needed for the teaching of רבי ינאי.
As רבי ינאי said: "You also":
just as you are members of the covenant,
so too your agents must be members of the covenant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by giving the extra words a new purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse to a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "גם אתם" has no purpose once agency for תרומה is learned from other cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: "גם אתם" teaches that the agent must be בני ברית.

steps.title: Isn't רבי ינאי's rule already known from רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: Why is a verse needed? רבי יוחנן already taught that an עבד cannot be an agent for a גט, since he is not part of the laws of גיטין and קידושין. The same logic should exclude a נכרי from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse for this? It comes from what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן. For רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A slave cannot become an agent to receive a גט from the woman's husband, because he is not included in the laws of divorce and קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 20. רבי ינאי's rule seems to follow from a general principle we already have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule suggests a principle: someone who is not part of a law cannot be an agent for that law. A נכרי is not commanded in תרומה, so this principle should already exclude him. That would make the verse unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out (it is derived from)
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
Included in the laws of divorce and קידושין

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse for this?

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָפְקָא!
phrases.english: It comes out from what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן!

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
A slave cannot become an agent

phrases.aramaic: לְקַבֵּל גֵּט מִיַּד בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: to receive a גט from the hand of the woman's husband,
because he is not included in the laws of divorce and קידושין.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְמָה לִי קְרָא? מִדְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the verse used in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for "גם אתם" to teach רבי ינאי's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's principle already excludes anyone who is not part of a law from being an agent for it.

steps.title: A נכרי is different, because his own תרומה counts
steps.stepSummary: The verse is needed. An עבד has no part in divorce at all, but a נכרי's own תרומה does count. So we might have thought he could also be an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: a slave cannot be an agent, because he has no ability to release a woman by divorce at all. But a non-Jew is included in his own תרומה, as we learned in a משנה: "A non-Jew or a כותי who separated תרומה, their תרומה is תרומה." So I would say he can also be an agent. The verse teaches us that he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן's rule is not enough. A נכרי has some connection to תרומה, so a verse is needed to exclude him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's case is an עבד, who has no connection at all to divorce. A נכרי is different, since תרומה he separates from his own produce does count. Because of this partial connection, we might have let him be an agent. "גם אתם" teaches that he still cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say
Someone who can permit (release) a woman by divorce

steps.whatToRemember: A נכרי cannot be a שליח to separate תרומה. This is learned from "גם אתם", even though a נכרי's own תרומה counts.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say a נכרי is commanded to give תרומה. It only says that if he does separate from his own produce, it counts. That is exactly why we might have mistakenly allowed him to be an agent.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
for it might have entered your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: עֶבֶד, דְּלָאו בַּר הֶיתֵּירָא הוּא כְּלָל.
phrases.english: A slave cannot, because he cannot release a woman at all.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נׇכְרִי, הוֹאִיל וְאִיתֵיהּ בִּתְרוּמָה דְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ,
phrases.english: But a non-Jew, since he is included in his own תרומה,
as we learned: a non-Jew or a כותי who separated תרומה,
their תרומה is תרומה,
I would say he can also act as an agent,
so the verse teaches us that he cannot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by showing that a נכרי's case is different from an עבד's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a נכרי has a partial connection to תרומה, but an עבד has no connection to divorce.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a נכרי's own תרומה counts, he could also be an agent for a Jew's תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "גם אתם" teaches that a נכרי cannot be an agent for תרומה, even though his own תרומה counts.

steps.title: According to רבי שמעון, why are the extra words needed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that a נכרי's תרומה is not real תרומה. So the reason given in step 22 does not work for him, and the words "אתם" and "גם אתם" seem unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון, who exempts: as we learned in a משנה, a נכרי's תרומה makes a mixture forbidden, and someone who eats it by mistake must pay an extra fifth, but רבי שמעון exempts him. So why do I need "you" and "you also"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 22 by bringing רבי שמעון, who holds that a נכרי's תרומה does not really count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said we needed the פסוק because a נכרי's own תרומה counts, so we might think he can also be an agent. רבי שמעון says a נכרי's תרומה does not count at all, so there was never a reason to think he could be an agent. For him, the words that teach that rule look unneeded again.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a mixture forbidden as תרומה (מדומע)
The extra fifth paid by a non-כהן who eats תרומה by mistake

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shimon, who exempts,
as we learned in a mishna:
The teruma of a gentile makes a mixture forbidden as teruma,
phrases.notes: If it falls into regular food, the whole mixture gets treated like תרומה.

phrases.english: and one is liable to pay an added fifth for it,
but Rabbi Shimon exempts.
Why do I need "you" and "you also"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 22 from the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 22 that the פסוק is needed because a נכרי's תרומה counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי שמעון, a נכרי's own תרומה has no קדושה, so he is like the עבד: not part of the law at all. רבי יוחנן's principle (step 21) already excludes him, so 'גם אתם' is not needed for רבי ינאי's rule.

steps.title: Without "גם" we would think "אתם" also excludes an agent
steps.stepSummary: The word "אתם" excludes several kinds of people from separating תרומה. Without "גם אתם" we might think it also excludes an agent, so the extra words teach that an agent is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since the Master said "you" and not sharecroppers, "you" and not partners, "you" and not a guardian, "you" and not one who separates תרומה from what is not his, then also "you" and not your agent. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, even for רבי שמעון, the words "גם אתם" are needed to teach that an agent can separate תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אתם" already keeps out many people who are not the real owner. Without more, we would have put an agent on that same list. "גם אתם" tells us that an agent is different, since he stands in place of the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecroppers who work someone else's field for a share of the crop
A guardian or steward who manages someone else's property
It would enter your mind (introduces a mistaken first thought)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two jobs here. "אתם" alone excludes people, while "גם אתם" includes the agent.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
since it would enter your mind to say:
Since the Master said:
"You," and not sharecroppers;
"you," and not partners;
"you," and not a guardian;
"you," and not one who separates teruma from what is not his;
I would say: "you," and also not your agent.
So it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: The extra word "גם" shows that an agent can separate תרומה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the words a new necessary job (including an agent) that works even for רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since "אתם" excludes sharecroppers, partners, guardians and non-owners, it would also exclude an agent.
steps.terutzMaskana: "גם אתם" teaches that an agent can separate תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: Even for רבי שמעון, "גם אתם" is needed. Without it, we would have thought an agent is excluded together with sharecroppers, partners and guardians.

steps.title: Where does רבי יונתן learn agency for קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The source for agency in קדשים works for רבי יהושע בן קרחה. רבי יונתן uses that פסוק for a different lesson, so where does he learn it from?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבי יהושע בן קרחה. But according to רבי יונתן, who uses this פסוק for a different teaching, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the basic source for agency in קדשים and asks how it works for רבי יונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for agency in קדשים came from a פסוק that רבי יהושע בן קרחה reads this way. If רבי יונתן needs that פסוק for a different lesson, he has no source yet for agency in קדשים. Since תרומה was learned from קדשים (step 18), this question matters for the whole chain.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion, but not for another)
Who takes it out (uses the פסוק) for
A different teaching learned from the פסוק
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa.
But according to Rabbi Yonatan,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהַאי קְרָא לִדְרָשָׁא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: who uses this verse for a different teaching,
from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה. אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה discussion and goes back to the root source for agency in קדשים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of agency in קדשים from the קרבן פסח פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That derivation only works if the פסוק is free for this lesson. רבי יונתן uses it for something else, so he still needs a source.
steps.whyThisMatters: תרומה and other cases lean on קדשים, so if קדשים has no source for רבי יונתן, the whole structure needs a new base.

steps.title: רבי יונתן's ברייתא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to show the other lesson that רבי יונתן learns from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן says, from where do we know that all of Israel can fulfill their obligation...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא begins quoting רבי יונתן's ברייתא to prove he uses the פסוק for a different lesson, and the quote continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא backs up the claim in step 25 that רבי יונתן reads the פסוק differently. He uses it to teach that all of Israel can fulfill their obligation in a certain way. Since the פסוק is busy with that lesson, it cannot also teach agency for him.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita, Rabbi Yonatan says:
From where do we know that all of Israel can fulfill their obligation

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that shows רבי יונתן's other reading mentioned in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יונתן uses the פסוק to teach how all of Israel can fulfill their obligation (the quote continues on the next עמוד).
